Quick triage notes (initial):
- I pulled their org/project identifiers from the logs: org_id=org-clearsight, project=cs-prod-94.
- Observed behavior in control plane: an automated policy job that reconciles project->tier labels mis-ran during midnight UTC maintenance and applied the org default tier label ("starter") to cs-prod-94. That label imposes a hard per-project QPS cap that's ~60% lower than their historical traffic for this job.
- When the job started at 02:00 UTC it immediately hit that cap; our edge returned 429s and their client retried aggressively which produced a retry storm and some upstream timeouts.

Evidence:
- Audit log: policy_reconcile_job ran 2027-04-24T00:01:12Z and assigned label tier=starter to project cs-prod-94 (we have the entry in control-plane-audit-logs).
- Metrics: their token-level QPS crossed the new per-project limit at 02:03 UTC, concurrent failures spiked to 18%.

Immediate remediation (recommended):
1) Roll back label assignment for cs-prod-94 to previous tier=enterprise (manual patch to label store) — ETA 20min. This will remove the tight per-project cap.
2) Apply a short-lived emergency override (10x rate window for 1 hour) to let in-flight jobs drain while we confirm stability.
3) Add a temporary client-side guidance: set exponential backoff with jitter in their retry policy (Grace / Marissa can coordinate messaging).

Longer-term fixes:
- Harden reconcile job to never downgrade a project if observed traffic in last 24h exceeds threshold.
- Add canary check: do not apply tier label changes to projects with active high-QPS in last hour.

I've kicked off the rollback; will post when complete and include the exact control-plane audit entries.

-Vivek

Andre —

Thank you for the quick report and the log bundle. I'm really sorry for the disruption. Summary of what we found and immediate actions we've taken: 

What happened:
- During a control-plane reconcile run at midnight UTC, a label reconciliation job incorrectly applied the org default tier label ("starter") to your project cs-prod-94. That tier imposes a much lower per-project rate cap than the ingest job typically uses.
- When your batch job started at 02:00 UTC it hit the new cap and received 429s. Your retry logic produced a retry storm which amplified load and produced some 5xx/timeouts.

What we did immediately:
- Rolled back the tier label assignment for cs-prod-94 back to tier=enterprise (completed at 10:24 PDT).
- Applied a one-hour emergency override to the project to allow queued traffic to drain (expires 12:24 PDT).
- Asked your team to temporarily apply exponential backoff with jitter while we stabilize.

Next steps and ETA:
- Engineering (Vivek) will monitor metrics for the next two hours to validate no residual retry waves — we'll post a confirmation by 13:30 PDT.
- Grace/Marissa will follow up with a short customer-facing postmortem and coordinates on account credits.
- We'll deliver a blameless RCA within 48 hours describing the policy change that caused the reconcile job to downgrade the project and the mitigation plan to prevent recurrence.

We understand this impacted your SLA and will make amends — we'll include service credit options in the follow-up. If you want us to temporarily pause the reconcile job for your org while we audit label rules, we can do that.

Appreciate the patience — we know this is urgent.
